description: ODC (coverage): the three types that live on the EDGES of an app — ISystemEvent (what the app does at startup), IExternalSite (the destination that leaves the app for the outside) and IEvent, the Extended Event (the DOM event that a widget hands to a screen action). They are three different traps. (1) ISystemEvent: the API has FOUR factories that return exactly that type (IESpace.CreateOnApplicationReady / CreateOnApplicationResume / CreateOnBeginWebRequest / CreateOnSessionStart) and none takes arguments, so the 'name' of the create is IGNORED and the job does NOT choose which one is born — the one that chooses is the reflection order (in this build it answers CreateOnApplicationReady). The only honest proof is to read the @espace back and see which of the five [Child] stopped being null, and that is what this job does. It is not a collection: the key is <espace>.#OnApplicationReady, a unique place per app. And, unlike the IRestServiceAction and the automatic process activity (AGENTS.md section 1), the flow is born EMPTY (Nodes=0, IsValid=False): not creating the Start gives Error InvalidFlow_NoStart, so Start, body, End, links and layout are all the author's work. To choose deterministically there is only IESpace.CreateOnSync(), which returns IOnSyncSystemEvent and no longer answers to the name ISystemEvent. (2) IExternalSite: it lives in the UI FLOW (it is an IMobileFlowNode), never inside a screen; the homonymous candidate from OutSystems.Model.UI.Web is discarded on its own by the generic constraint of IMobileFlow.CreateNode<T>, so the bare name is enough. What the platform does on its own: it gives it a default position on the canvas and maintains HasURLParameter, a READONLY property derived from InputParameters.Any(input => input.Name == "URL") — creating an IInputParameter called URL makes it become True with no set, and that is the shape production external sites have. What does NOT follow: that default position is the SAME for all (the two external sites of this job are born overlapping at 3196,800, the same point ui-flow-comment.json shows for the Comment) — and the point belongs to the node TYPE, not to the flow: the screen created here, in the same MainFlow, is born at 1000,1000. And nothing links the node to anyone: an orphan external site raises not ONE Verify message, whoever wants it reachable has to point a Destination at it. (3) IEvent: the type is called IEvent but the object is the Extended Event and it has no writable Name — it is born without a name (DisplayName 'Extended Event') and starts being called by the event itself as soon as Event is written: the second derived property of this job. 'Event' is a CLOSED list of 11 names read from the product (NRWebWidgets.cs, AbstractTopLevelWidget.DefaultExtendedEventNames: onblur, onchange, onclick, ondoubleclick, onfocus, onkeydown, onkeypress, onkeyup, ontouchstart, ontouchmove, ontouchend) and without it comes Error RequiredPropertyValue_Property 'Event must be set'. 'Handler' appears in API V1 as IObject, but the real descriptor is DestinationPropertyDescriptor<ExtendedEvent, IExecutableWebDestinationWithNoOutputs> (ExtendedEvent.cs, with the text 'JavaScript event handler.'): only an action WITHOUT outputs gets in there, and a screen action qualifies because it has none. The parent does not need to be a container: here an IContainer and an IInput carry different events with the same handler. The usages sorts out the whole family: the extended event handler counts as IEvent, the Destination of the button counts as IBuiltinEvent — they are two event families on the same widget, and only the builtin one navigates.

mandatory: without this node Verify returns Error InvalidFlow_NoStart 'Start is required in OnApplicationReady'

the complete flow that the AUTHOR had to assemble: Start with connector, Assign with Assignment and connector, End. None of this came for free

the IEvent is a child of the CONTAINER (Events collection), next to the content and the Visible expression; the second event is deeper, inside the IInput
count=real=2, byType IEvent:2 — the two extended events are REAL consumers of the screen action, and that is why it does not show up as UnusedAction even with no button calling it
